snippet.title: Alex Honnold Freesolos Taipei 101 🧗
snippet.description:
So this guy just climbed one of the world's tallest buildings without any safety gear.

You see, Alex Honnold is a world-class climber famous for "free soloing."
Free soloing means climbing with no safety gear whatsoever. 

This means - one wrong move - and you fall to your death. 

His latest project was Taipei 101: a 1600 foot megastructure located in Taiwan but there was just one problem: Alex has trained his entire life on rock which has cracks, edges, and texture but this building was completely covered in smooth glass.

He survived by locking his fingers onto the narrow metal beams between glass panels, climbing the building section by section like a human spider.
The climb was so controlled that he actually paused mid-ascent to wave at spectators watching through the windows.

He reached the top in just 90 minutes, setting the record for the biggest urban free solo of all time.

snippet.title: The World’s Coldest City ❄️😮
snippet.description:
What is life like in the coldest city in the world?

You see, the coldest city in the world is Yakutsk, Russia where winter temperatures regularly hit −40°C to −60°C.

At these temperatures exposed skin can freeze in minutes, so people dress in thick layers, and plan every step outside.

The cold is also problematic for cars - causing engine oil to thicken and batteries to lose their charge so many vehicles are left running or plugged in all day and night during the winter months.

Food changes too. People rely on high-fat, high-protein meals like frozen fish and raw frozen horse meat, often refrigerated outside. 

Despite these crazy conditions, over 300,000 people still live there.

snippet.title: How do snakes swallow animals so much bigger than they are? - Niko Zlotnik
snippet.description:
Explore how snakes evolved, and find out how their jaw-dropping anatomy allows them to take down prey several times their size.

--

Since slithering onto the scene some 150 million years ago, evolving length and limbless-ness out of their ancestral lizard forms, snakes have diversified rapidly. Their noodly bodies and flexible heads granted them access to novel places and prey. And today, there are nearly 4,000 snake species, spanning habitats high and low. Niko Zlotnik explores how snakes evolved into incredible predators.

snippet.title: The longest Marathon In Human History 🏃
snippet.description:
In 1912, a Japanese runner named Shizo Kanakuri was selected to compete in the Stockholm Olympics.

But Getting to Sweden took weeks by boat and train. So By race day, Kanakuri was exhausted, and malnourished.

The race was held in the middle of a heatwave. Which led to Shizo collapsing mid race from severe dehydration. 

He was taken in by a local Swedish family who helped him recover.

However Shizo was Ashamed of failing, so he quietly returned to Japan without telling Olympic officials - and for decades, Sweden listed him as a missing person.

Then, in 1967, Swedish television tracked him down and invited him back to Stockholm to finally finish the race.

At 75 years old, Kanakuri stepped onto the track and crossed the finish line.

His official time? 54 years, 8 months, 6 days, 5 hours, 32 minutes, 20 seconds and 10 grand children.

snippet.description:

Without any real atmosphere to burn up incoming space rocks, building habitats deep inside these ancient lava tubes provides crucial protection against the non-stop threat of meteorite bombardments. These subterranean shelters also perfectly solve the Moon's brutal temperature swings, completely insulating future colonists from the punishing 250-degree Fahrenheit daytime heat and the freezing negative 208-degree nights. snippet.title: The dark origins of Disney fairy tales - Claudia Schwabe

An evil stepmother demands a maiden’s lungs and liver; a girl is ripped from a wolf’s stomach; and sisters mutilate their feet to squeeze into a gold slipper. During the early 1800s, brothers Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm gathered these unflinchingly gory details from stories circulating around what’s now Germany. Claudia Schwabe explores how these now-infamous tales evolved as they spread worldwide.

localized.title: The dark origins of Disney fairy tales - Claudia Schwabe
localized.description:
Dig into the infamous tales of the Brothers Grimm, and explore how these gory stories evolved as they spread around the world.

--

An evil stepmother demands a maiden’s lungs and liver; a girl is ripped from a wolf’s stomach; and sisters mutilate their feet to squeeze into a gold slipper. During the early 1800s, brothers Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm gathered these unflinchingly gory details from stories circulating around what’s now Germany. Claudia Schwabe explores how these now-infamous tales evolved as they spread worldwide.

Lesson by Claudia Schwabe, directed by Skirmanta Jakaitė.
